cards.text: Last chapter of Hebrews, friend! The writer just told his readers they're receiving a kingdom that can't be shaken (Hebrews 12:28), and now he rolls up his sleeves and gets practical. His first line is four words long: “Continue in brotherly love.”

cards.question: Next the writer says, don't neglect to show hospitality to strangers. His reason? By doing that, some people have entertained ___ without knowing it.

cards.text: Then he turns to the folks having the hardest week of anybody: “Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated as if you were suffering with them.” Not a quick “thinking of you” text, friend, but AS IF you were RIGHT THERE with them.

cards.question: The writer says to remember prisoners only if they were locked up for their faith.

cards.text: Next topic: marriage, and the writer does NOT tiptoe around it. He says God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.

cards.question: The writer says marriage should be honored only by the people who are married.

cards.text: “Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have,” the writer says. Content with what you HAVE, friend, coming from a guy who lived in a junk drawer and STILL wanted a nicer spot behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: So why can a person be content with what they have, according to the writer?

answers.text: God has said He will never leave them
Money always runs out in the end
Their reward is coming very soon

cards.question: Because the Lord is their helper, the writer says believers can say with confidence that they will not be afraid of what man can do to them.

cards.text: Now he points them to their leaders, the ones who spoke the word of God to them. Look at how those leaders' lives turned out, he says.

cards.question: Consider the outcome of your leaders' way of life, the writer says, and ___ their faith.

cards.text: Then comes a line I'd stamp on every cookie in my bakery: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” I've changed my sprinkle ratio four times since breakfast, friend, and He hasn't changed ONCE.

cards.question: Next, the writer warns his readers not to get carried away. Carried away by what?
It's good for the heart to be strengthened by ___, the writer says, and not by foods of no value to those devoted to them.

cards.text: Then he says, “We have an altar from which those who serve at the tabernacle have no right to eat.” And he points back to the high priest, who brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, while the bodies are burned outside the camp.

cards.question: The writer says Jesus also suffered, to sanctify the people by His own blood. Where did He suffer?
So the writer says, let us go to Jesus outside the camp. What do we carry with us?
The writer says believers already have a permanent city here.

cards.text: Instead, he says, we are looking for the city that is to come. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, I KNOW a temporary address when I see one.
The writer's been talking about sacrifices and altars. Now he names one anybody can offer to God through Jesus, continually, and friend, it doesn't even need an oven.

cards.question: Through Jesus, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of ___, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
The writer names more sacrifices that please God. Which ones?

answers.text: Doing good and sharing with others

cards.text: Then he comes back to leaders: obey them and submit to them, because they watch over your souls. Being that leader is like being the one person in the group chat who actually reads EVERY message.

cards.question: The writer says leaders watch over souls as people who must do what?
The writer says it does the people no good when their leaders lead with grief instead of joy.

cards.text: Now the writer gets personal: “Pray for us.” He says they're convinced they have a clear conscience and want to live honorably in every way.

cards.question: What does the writer especially urge his readers to pray for?

answers.text: That he may be restored to them soon
That his letter will reach every church
That his enemies will be stopped

cards.text: Then the writer starts a blessing: “Now may the God of peace…” He describes God as the One who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep.

cards.question: The writer says God brought Jesus back from the dead through something. What?

answers.text: The blood of the eternal covenant

cards.question: The writer's blessing: may the God of peace ___ you with every good thing to do His ___.

cards.text: He asks God to accomplish in us what is pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ, “to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.” That's how you close the oven door on a perfect batch, friend.
Then he adds a little P.S. for the road. He urges his brothers to bear with his word of exhortation.

cards.question: The writer tells his readers his letter is long, so they should be patient with it.

cards.text: THIRTEEN chapters, and the man calls it BRIEF, which is like me saying I'll only sample ONE chocolate chip. Then he shares some news about Timothy, whom he calls our brother.

cards.question: What's the news the writer shares about Timothy?
If Timothy arrives soon, the writer plans to come see his readers together with him.

cards.text: Then come the greetings: “Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.”

cards.question: The very last line of the whole letter: ___ be with all of you.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 7 quotes "Pray for us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of Hebrews 13:2 (entertained ___ without knowing it). No earlier card sets up anything the baker could reason from, so picking angels over kings or prophets is a guess at unseen wording, not at meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to Papa Dorin's backstory: that in the junk drawer he wanted a nicer spot behind the takeout menus. The backstory never says this. It also clashes with it, since in the drawer he gave up on himself and then spent his time welcoming newcomers. Jokes may invent small moments around his bakery, not new drawer history.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'All kinds of worldly riches' is arguable. Hebrews 13:5 has just warned the readers to keep their lives free from the love of money, so a baker could argue that being carried away by riches is something the writer warns against in this passage.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'law' for the second blank is too close to the right answer 'will'. A baker could argue that 'to do His law' means close to the same thing as 'to do His will'.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This is Timothy's first appearance. He is introduced only as someone the writer calls 'our brother', which doesn't tell the baker who Timothy is. A short identifier with its reference is needed, for example Paul's coworker (Acts 16:1-3).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the first word of the letter's final line (___ be with all of you). It tests the exact wording of the closing blessing, not meaning that can be reasoned out. Wisdom or Strength would fit just as well without having seen the text.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
